tasks.short: Reconcile bank statements with payment records and cleared cheque evidence where cheques remain.

steps.what: Download bank movements for the reconciliation period.
Retrieve payment postings and available cleared cheque references.
Compare references and amounts, separating timing differences from unmatched movements.
Investigate missing evidence, duplicate postings and unexplained amounts.
Review reconciliation evidence and authorise corrections.
Post authorised corrections and file the reconciliation evidence.

tasks.design: Configure matching in the {ERP}, using a {BANK} feed and a small {DATA_PLATFORM} connector for missing payment references. A {WORKFLOW} queue holds exceptions and correction approvals; only the exact approved correction is posted, with evidence retained in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Disconnected exports and missing references left a spreadsheet between bank records and accounting records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching rules handle clean records. AI-assisted coding can shorten connector development, but access and testing still take time.
tasks.still_hard: Unreadable cheque images, partial payments and unexplained differences need investigation. GDPR requires controlled access and appropriate retention.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk distinguishes a timing difference from an accounting error and finds evidence across teams.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of unresolved bank reconciliation exceptions

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time comparing rows and more time clearing unexplained movements. With delegated limits, they can prioritise investigations each day; the accountant retains correction approval.

reach.task: Prepare bank reconciliation evidence for period close
reach.learn: Cut-off rules, clearing accounts and evidence required for correcting journals
Bank value dates, settlement timing and cash reporting

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can match bank lines by reference, IBAN or invoice number and send misses to a person.
Structured matching and approved journal posting can use deterministic rules; cheque images may remain exceptions.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Bank reconciliation is common; cancelled cheque handling is a conditional legacy branch in European companies.
The baseline uses a spreadsheet to bridge bank and accounting records.
Structured references cover routine matches; image-only evidence goes to a person.
Build ranges cover one bank connection and one accounting entity.
Normal billing automation does not introduce employee monitoring. Any consultation requirement depends on national rules and the actual change.
unknowns: Whether cheques are used and cleared cheque evidence is available
Existing matching features, bank interfaces and access rights
Actual exception volumes, task time and approval limits
Required retention periods and employee consultation arrangements
research_questions: Which bank statement formats expose stable transaction and cheque references?
Can configured matching prevent ambiguous and duplicate matches before marking records reconciled?
new_work: Review ambiguous matches and missing evidence
Maintain reference mappings and matching tolerances
Monitor feed completeness and failed imports
Check that posted corrections match their approved versions

tasks.short: Route customer statements to approved electronic, postal or counter delivery channels.

steps.what: Select prepared customer statements for the dispatch batch.
Check recipient details and recorded delivery preferences.
Resolve missing addresses, conflicting preferences and uncertain recipients.
Prepare electronic queues, postal bundles or counter collection packs.
Send statements to verified electronic recipients.
Mail physical statements or hand collection packs to identified customers.
Record dispatch completion and flag failed delivery.

tasks.design: Configure statement routing in the {ERP} using verified contacts and delivery preferences from the {CRM}. A {WORKFLOW} queue holds uncertain recipients, prepares physical dispatch packs and records delivery failures; routine electronic statements leave through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact details, preferences and dispatch records were maintained separately. Physical preparation obscured which routing work could be automated.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing statement queues, templates and routing rules can cover most preparation. Small connectors can synchronise verified preferences.
tasks.still_hard: Physical handling remains where customers require it. Wrong-recipient disclosure requires careful identity and routing controls under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk resolves uncertain recipient authority and helps customers who need another delivery channel.
tasks.altitude: The clerk handles failed deliveries and uncertain recipients instead of sorting every statement. No new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Resolve statement delivery failures before collection contact
reach.learn: Delivery evidence, customer contact verification and the difference between delivery failure and non-payment

evidence.claim: Configured queues can route prepared statements using structured recipient and channel records.
Routing and preparation can be automated even when physical delivery remains human.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Prepared statements already exist; this task covers routing and dispatch.
The baseline includes electronic and physical delivery. Counter collection applies only where offered.
Routine electronic dispatch is authorised by existing policy and uses verified recipient records.
The human-class prior understates gains in routing and preparation; physical handling remains human.
GDPR applies to customer records. Consultation depends on national rules if the change affects employees.
unknowns: Actual channel mix and whether counter delivery exists
How recipient authority and delivery preferences are verified
Existing dispatch features and contact synchronisation
Physical handling volumes, delivery costs and employee consultation requirements
research_questions: Can existing routing rules bind each statement to its customer identifier and verified destination?
Which delivery failure signals can be captured without treating successful sending as confirmed receipt?
new_work: Review uncertain recipients and returned statements
Maintain channel preferences and routing rules
Monitor failed sends and incomplete physical dispatch logs
Check document-to-recipient pairing after template changes

tasks.short: Correct mistaken cheque returns, arrange return or retrieval, and explain account adjustments.

steps.what: Register the reported cheque return error.
Gather cheque details, bank status, correspondence and account postings.
Compare payment evidence and calculate the proposed account correction.
Approve the correction and decide whether to return or retrieve the cheque.
Post the authorised adjustment to the customer account.
Arrange the authorised physical return or retrieval and record custody.
Prepare an explanation of the error, adjustment and next action.

loop.input: Approved case facts, posted adjustment, custody status and an explanation template
loop.output: A customer explanation draft with references to supporting records
loop.check: Validate every amount, date and status against the records; the clerk checks wording before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair, with a 2,000-token total budget. Missing facts use a manual template.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case histories and customer questions vary in free text. Arithmetic and posting remain deterministic.

steps.what: Answer the customer, confirm next steps and handle disputed facts.
Update the case with the response, custody outcome and unresolved issues.

tasks.design: Use a case record in the {ERP} and a {WORKFLOW} queue to collect {BANK} evidence, calculate corrections and capture approval of the exact posting and cheque instruction. A bounded drafting loop prepares explanations from approved facts in {DOCS}; the clerk sends the response and people handle physical custody.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rare cases cross bank records, correspondence, accounting corrections and physical custody. Their small volume rarely justified a separate application.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured case records and approval flows can reuse existing infrastructure. A bounded model loop can draft explanations without deciding the remedy.
tasks.still_hard: Actual cheque recovery, disputed ownership and incomplete custody evidence remain difficult. GDPR, national cheque rules and authorisation limits govern handling; AI Act literacy applies to model use.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk earns cooperation, resolves disputed facts and explains a financial error without making unsupported promises.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling evidence and writing explanations, and more time resolving disputed cases. No new adjustment or settlement authority is assumed.

reach.task: Prepare evidence for a customer account correction
reach.learn: Reversal journals, suspense balances and prevention of duplicate refunds
Evidence preservation, custody records and escalation thresholds

evidence.claim: Case records can join evidence, authorised corrections and custody outcomes without automating remedy decisions.
A bounded loop can draft record-grounded explanations while a person controls external responses.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: This is a conditional legacy task. Many mid-size European companies have no customer cheque return process.
The shares describe a case where this task exists, rather than a typical share of the whole job.
A supervisor can approve corrections within delegated limits; larger cases escalate.
Automatic posting consumes the exact approved correction and prevents duplicate execution.
The drafting loop is used only if reusable templates cannot handle the observed case variety.
Consultation requirements depend on national rules and any change to employee working arrangements.
unknowns: Whether cheque returns occur and whether their volume justifies a build
Who holds cheque custody and who can authorise account adjustments
Available bank status data and existing case features
Customer authentication, retention rules and employee consultation requirements
research_questions: Can the existing case system preserve approval history and custody evidence without a custom application?
Do evaluated drafts preserve uncertain facts and avoid inventing recovery dates or promises?
Which national rules govern cheque return and retrieval in the operating countries?
new_work: Review drafted explanations and unsupported statements
Maintain correction templates and approval limits
Monitor duplicate-posting controls and connector failures
Evaluate whether rare cases still justify the drafting loop

tasks.short: Record cheque stop requests, obtain authorisation and confirm the bank's response.

steps.what: Record the stop-payment request and its stated reason.
Verify requester authority, cheque identity and current payment status.
Assess the reason and authorise or reject the stop instruction.
Submit the approved stop instruction through the bank's authorised procedure.
Record the bank's acceptance, rejection or pending status.
Notify affected finance staff and flag unresolved or rejected stops.

tasks.design: Configure a stop-payment form and approval queue in {WORKFLOW}, using cheque details from the {ERP} and status evidence from the {BANK}. An authorised person submits the bank instruction, then records the acknowledgement; {WORKFLOW} updates the internal register and notifies the finance team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived as loose messages, while bank authority and payment status remained in separate records. An internal notice could be confused with a completed bank stop.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms, approval records and automatic notifications can remove repeated copying. They do not depend on a new bank write interface.
tasks.still_hard: A cheque may clear before the bank acts, and an acknowledgement may only confirm receipt. Bank procedures, GDPR and national cheque rules still apply.
tasks.human_edge: The treasury approver weighs the reason, consequences and urgency; the bank operator verifies the exact instruction.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying instructions and chasing acknowledgements. The treasury approver and authorised bank operator retain their existing decision rights.

reach.task: Track pending and rejected stop-payment instructions
reach.learn: Bank cut-offs, acknowledgement states and authorised bank procedures
Segregation of duties, approval traceability and national cheque rules

evidence.claim: Structured requests, approval queues and notifications can reduce copying while bank submission remains human.
An internal stop notice does not itself stop a bank payment; submission and bank outcome require separate records.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: This is a conditional cheque process, not a routine task in every European company.
The bank accepts stop instructions through an authorised procedure; no write API is assumed.
Prepared instructions assist bank entry, while submission remains manual.
The approval in the case authorises the exact bank action; any required bank dual approval also remains.
Existing cheque identifiers support lookup; stale or missing status requires a person.
Employee consultation depends on national rules and the working arrangements affected.
unknowns: Whether cheque stops occur and how urgent they are
The bank's procedure, fees, cut-offs and acknowledgement meanings
Available cheque status data and access rights
Applicable employee consultation and retention requirements
research_questions: What bank evidence distinguishes a received instruction from an effective stop?
Can the configured workflow escalate pending cases before the relevant bank cut-off?
Which national rules govern stop instructions in the operating countries?
new_work: Review stale payment status and mismatched identifiers
Follow up pending or rejected bank instructions
Maintain signatory lists and approval limits
Reconcile internal stop notices with bank outcomes
Update procedures when bank cut-offs or channels change

role.altitude: The role shifts from copying and comparing records toward payment exceptions, delivery failures and evidence quality. Routine preparation becomes automatic; financial corrections and sensitive bank actions retain explicit approval.
reach: Accountants: prepare close evidence and supported correction journals
Treasurers: track unexplained cash movements and pending bank instructions
Bill and account collectors: resolve delivery failures before collection contact
Compliance officers: assemble traceable approval and custody records
skills_to_grow: Correction journals and segregation of duties
Bank status interpretation and payment cut-offs
GDPR data handling and AI Act literacy
role.ambitious_version: Become a payment exception specialist who prioritises unresolved movements daily and supplies reliable evidence to accounting and treasury. Validate cheque volumes first; where these legacy tasks are absent, remove their procedures and avoid building dedicated tools.
